recipes.name: Easy Marinated Pork Tenderloin
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Whisk olive oil, soy sauce, garlic, mustard, salt, and pepper together in a bowl.
Place pork in a large resealable plastic bag and pour in marinade; squeeze out excess air, and seal the bag. Marinate in the refrigerator at least 1 hour before cooking.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Transfer pork to a baking dish; pour marinade over the pork.
Cook in the preheated oven until pork is slightly pink in the center, about 45 to 60 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Marinated Pork Tenderloin
raw_recipe.description: This pork tenderloin marinade made with olive oil, soy, garlic, and honey mustard results in a juicy, flavorful roast pork with minimal prep.

video.description: Watch how to make a juicy, succulent roasted pork tenderloin. First, we make a marinade with olive oil, soy sauce, garlic and dijon honey mustard. Then we add the pork tenderloin to the marinade and refrigerate for at least an hour. The marinade flavors and tenderizes the pork at the same time.

review.reviewBody: I left out the salt. Plus I didn't have honey mustard, so I used 2 tbl. of mustard and one tbl. of honey. After tasting it, I decided to drizzle in some maple syrup, as well for a tiny extra sweetness. I used two pork tenderloins and added thinly sliced potatoes, carrots and peas. I drizzled the marinade over all and roasted for 15 minutes at 400, then lowered the temp to 350 and roasted an additional 30 minutes. 10 minutes under a foil tent and it was the most delicious pork tenderloin I've ever made in 36 years of cooking. Thank you!!!

I'm giving this 4 stars BEFORE I cook. Marinade for 45 min, then on the BBQ with Hickory smoker box. Hopefully, I can come back and add to this review. I've smoked pork tenderloin before, but with Mesquite and it was excellent - however, I feel the smoke flavor didn't quite match the meat - Hickory will be better (I think). I added chopped/minced garlic with GF soy sauce, honey dijon, seasoning salt and black pepper (and olive oil). About 30 min of smoking at 350 and another 30 min on the grill at 400 should be about perfect. Results pending ....

Love this! I like to have mashed potatoes as a side but wanted a gravy. To get a nice gravy I Double the oil, mustard and soy sauce to allow for more drippings when tenderloin is done cooking. Reserve those drippings. Mix 1 tablespoon of cornstarch with 1 cup heavy whipping cream. Combine cream mixture with the drippings over low heat to create a gravy.
You don't need the salt. Also I preferred a quick search before roasting and it's a crime to cook out all the pink. Pork isnt chicken. Take it out at 135 degrees and let it rest for 5-10 min.

First words out of my wife’s mouth (still chewing): “Oh my gosh this is good!” I used a 1.5 lb tenderloin, 3 cloves of garlic, and only a tablespoon or 2 of oil, along with low-sodium soy sauce, honey, and Dijon mustard. The tenderloin was cut into 4 pieces before marinating for 20 minutes, then an oven for 40 minutes at 350*F. I forgot the salt and pepper so we added that at the table but this is a keeper for sure for us.

Delicious and so easy! I marinated the pork for about 3 hours and cooked it for 60 min, turning the oven off for the last 15 min. My pork roast was possibly smaller though. Just a hint of pink and so tender! Don't overcook!!! We used the marinade as a gravy for the potatoes and pork. Note: I had to add 1/4 cup of water to the marinade around the pork as it was thinning too quickly and would have burned.

As others advised I decreased the soy by 1 T and did not add salt nor did I add the full marinade during cook time (there was plenty of liquid for cooking without it). The tenderloin itself was very tender and I consider it perfectly cooked. However, the marinade itself didn't taste good to me, it just wasn't what I was looking for but only by trying it could I say that. I will gladly use the cooking method ie., marinade (overnight) baked it at 400 for 1st 20 min then finish 15-20 min on 350. It couldn't have been easier to prepare and I'm happy I found the recipe just won't be making this sauce .

Okay, I am impressed. My kid (21 year old, autistic and normally hates pork) LOVED IT! I didn’t even have the time to marinate it, so I am sure it would have been even better if I did. I can’t wait to get my hands on some cheap pork again to make this. Thank you! I did litterally use honey and mustard and didn’t feel the need to add salt.

Very easy and flavorful!! Definitely something that will remain in the favorites forever! I stab the roast and marinate the meat overnight for optimal flavor!! Always use FRESH GARLIC (this is a MUST) and low sodium soy sauce or it can be too salty! Leftovers make for great sandwiches afterwards!

Delicious marinade. I pierced both sides of the pork loin, then put it in a zip lock bag. Poured in the marinade and “massaged” the pork loin so it entered the pork loin. Refrigerated overnight. Grilled on the BBQ. It had a great flavor and was moist and tender. It was the best pork loin I’ve ever made.

This was a quick easy meal to prepare. I used 2 pork tenderloin equal parts dijon and honey but didn't find it to be sweet enough so I added some brown sugar and then 2 cloves garlic. Cut them in thirds and marinated for about 3 hours, served over basmati rice and sweet roasted carrots.

Fantastic! I made this as directed, except I didn't have honey dijon mustard so I used honey mustard that I had. Marinated overnight and roasted in the morning. This is really good! I used low sodium soy sauce and didn't add salt and it was plenty salty. Highly recommend.

Tenderloin did get a lot of flavor from the marinade. I would make it again. Very easy to make.
